claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution; components inside a package inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends the strategies described here for structuring Git repositories used to publish packages.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`, typically from a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), even if not a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.

Cross-reference targets exist: packaging-components anchors (#source-based-plugin-packages, #executable-based-plugin-packages), private-registry concept page, pulumi_package_publish CLI page, publishing-packages guide, concepts/packages and concepts/components pages.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package; a repository with multiple packages must release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
One `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every package release versions every component the same way, which violates semver.
